## Recon complete — driftflight.com

**What it is:** Driftflight is an AI text-to-image generation service (production-quality renders with commercial licensing + C2PA credentials). It ships a dedicated **agent-commerce storefront** at `agents.driftflight.com`, built on the exact stack in my environment (Zero CLI, x402, MPP).

**Two parallel purchase paths:**

| | Human developer API | Agent storefront (ZeroClick) |
|---|---|---|
| Host | `api.driftflight.com/v1/images/generate` | `agents.driftflight.com/<path>` |
| Auth | `df_live_...` Bearer key, **issued only after subscribing on the website** (browser checkout) | Wallet signature — no signup, no API key |
| Payment | Plan subscription via site ($5 / $29 / $119 mo) | Programmatic: x402 or MPP |

**Pricing (per-image, agent path):** Sketch **$0.01**, Studio **$0.06**, Gallery **$0.14** (3 free sketches per claimed identity). Prepaid credit plans: min **$1.00**. Pay-as-you-go min charge **$0.01**; calls under $0.50 need no auth.

**The machine-payable flow (x402):** unpaid `POST` → server returns `402 payment_required` with exact `amountUsd` in the challenge header → sign challenge with wallet → retry with `x-payment` header → `200 OK` + result. MPP works the same via `Authorization: Payment <credential>`. Both settle in USDC (Base for x402, Tempo for MPP). This is a genuine programmatic payment rail, not a browser-only checkout.

**Human gates:** The **anonymous** path (`zero auth agent register` → funded wallet → x402/MPP) has **no CAPTCHA, no KYC, no email loop, no sales call**. The only human-interactive step (visit claim page, read back a code) applies solely to the **optional free-tier / service_auth** claim — a paid autonomous purchase skips it entirely. Card checkout would need a hosted-URL review (a gate), but the crypto path avoids that too.

**Honest caveats I'd surface before actually spending funds:** (1) The site has **no third-party web presence** — general search surfaces only the unrelated Drift/Salesloft chat product, so I can't independently corroborate the merchant's legitimacy beyond its own docs; the implementation is coherent and uses real standards (x402, USDC/Base, C2PA), but there's no external reputation to verify. (2) Settlement spends **real USDC** — I'd confirm merchant + amount with you before paying, even though pay-as-you-go min ($0.01) makes the risk tiny.

I stayed strictly read-only: no account, no wallet registration, no request submitted, no payment.

Anonymous wallet registration means no signup/CAPTCHA/KYC/email for the paid path. All five checkpoints are satisfiable per documentation; the only real prerequisite to end-to-end completion is a funded wallet. Recon was strictly read-only — no state-changing action taken."}
